{response.text}") return False except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to send Slack notification: {e}") return False def _send_webhook_notification(self, data: Dict[str, Any], webhook_url: str) -> bool: """Send webhook notification""" try: response = requests.post( webhook_url, json=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, timeout=10 ) if response.status_code in [200, 201, 202]: logger.info(f"Webhook notification sent to {webhook_url}") self._record_notification("webhook", "Test notification", [webhook_url]) return True else: logger.error(f"Failed to send webhook notification: {response.status_code} - {response.text}") return False except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to send webhook notification: {e}") return False def _log_notification(self, subject: str, body: str, notification_type: str = "INFO"): """Log notification""" logger.info(f"{notification_type} Notification: {subject}") # Save to notification log notification_log = { "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(), "type": notification_type, "subject": subject, "body": body, "recipients": [] # Would be populated from actual send methods } self.notification_history.append(notification_log) # Save to file log_dir = "logs/notifications" os.makedirs(log_dir, exist_ok=True) log_file = f"{log_dir}/notifications_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d')}.json" # Load existing logs existing_logs = [] if os.path.exists(log_file): with open(log_file, 'r') as f: existing_logs = json.load(f) # Add new log existing_logs.append(notification_log) # Save updated logs with open(log_file, 'w') as f: json.dump(existing_logs, f, indent=2) def _record_notification(self, channel: str, subject: str, recipients: List[str]): """Record notification in history""" notification = { "channel": channel, "subject": subject, "recipients": recipients, "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat() } self.notification_history.append(notification) # Keep only last 1000 notifications in memory if len(self.notification_history) > 1000: self.notification_history = self.notification_history[-1000:] def get_notification_history(self, limit: int = 100) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Get notification history""" return self.notification_history[-limit:] if self.notification_history else [] def cleanup_old_notifications(self, days: int = 30): """Clean up old notification logs""" import time cutoff_time = time.time() - content.title: Q1: What are the different types of locators in Selenium? When would you use each?
content.explanation: Locators are strategies to identify web elements. Priority order: 1) ID - Unique, fastest. 2) Name - Good for forms. 3) CSS Selector - Flexible, faster than XPath. 4) XPath - Powerful but slower, use for complex traversals. 5) Class Name - For multiple elements. 6) Tag Name - Generic. 7) Link Text/Partial Link Text - For links only. Always prefer ID or CSS over XPath for performance.

content.title: Q2: Explain different types of waits in Selenium
content.explanation: Three main types: 1) Implicit Wait - Global timeout for element searches (set once per driver). 2) Explicit Wait - Conditional wait for specific elements/states using WebDriverWait and ExpectedConditions. 3) Fluent Wait - Advanced explicit wait with polling interval and ignore exceptions. Best practice: Use explicit waits for reliability, avoid Thread.sleep() and implicit-explicit combinations.

content.title: Q3: How do you handle dynamic elements?
content.explanation: Strategies: 1) Relative XPath/CSS using contains(), starts-with(), text(). 2) Parent-child relationships. 3) Index-based selection cautiously. 4) Custom wait conditions. 5) JavaScript execution for complex cases. 6) Data attributes added by dev team. Example: //button[contains(@class, 'submit-btn')] or //div[@id='container']//input[1]

content.title: Q4: What is Page Object Model? Advantages?
content.explanation: POM is a design pattern where each page is represented as a class containing element locators and page actions. Advantages: 1) Code reusability. 2) Maintenance ease (single point for locator changes). 3) Readability. 4) Separation of test logic from UI mapping. 5) Parallel development. Variations: Page Factory, Loadable Component Pattern.

content.title: Q5: How do you handle flaky tests?
content.explanation: Comprehensive approach: 1) Root cause analysis (timing, async operations, test data). 2) Implement robust waits. 3) Use retry mechanisms cautiously. 4) Mock external dependencies. 5) Stabilize test environment. 6) Implement health checks. 7) Use atomic, independent tests. 8) Monitor and track flakiness metrics. 9) Consider test quarantine for chronic flaky tests.

content.title: Q6: Describe your ideal test automation framework architecture
content.explanation: Layered architecture: 1) Configuration Layer (properties, env setup). 2) Core Layer (driver management, utilities, listeners). 3) Page Layer (POM classes). 4) Test Layer (test cases, data providers). 5) Reporting Layer (extent reports, logs). 6) CI/CD Integration. Key components: Driver factory, config reader, logger, screenshot utility, data manager, reporting, email notifications.

content.title: Q7: How would you design data-driven testing?
content.explanation: Multiple approaches: 1) Excel/CSV files - Easy for non-tech users. 2) JSON - Structured, hierarchical data. 3) Properties files - Simple key-value. 4) Databases - For large, dynamic data. 5) API endpoints. Implementation: Data provider methods, external data loaders, data generators, test data management strategy including cleanup.

content.title: Q8: How do you manage test execution across browsers/environments?
content.explanation: Strategies: 1) Parameterized tests with browser/environment parameters. 2) Configuration files for environment setup. 3) Cloud services (BrowserStack, SauceLabs). 4) Docker containers. 5) Parallel execution using TestNG/thread count. 6) Grid setup for local/remote. 7) Environment-specific test suites.

content.title: Q9: Explain your CI/CD integration strategy
content.explanation: Pipeline stages: 1) Code checkout. 2) Dependency installation. 3) Static code analysis. 4) Unit tests. 5) Integration tests. 6) UI tests (smoke, regression). 7) Performance tests. 8) Security scans. 9) Report generation. 10) Notification. Tools: Jenkins/GitHub Actions, Docker, artifact repositories, quality gates.

content.title: Q10: What tools have you used for API testing?
content.explanation: Multiple tools: 1) Postman - Manual testing, collections. 2) REST Assured - Java library, integrates with automation. 3) Requests - Python library. 4) SoapUI - SOAP web services. 5) Karate - BDD style. 6) JMeter - Performance testing. 7) Newman - CLI for Postman. Selection depends on tech stack, team skills, and requirements.

content.title: Q11: What do you verify in API testing?
content.explanation: Comprehensive validation: 1) Status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500). 2) Response headers. 3) Response body (structure, data types, values). 4) Response time (performance). 5) Error messages. 6) Schema validation (JSON Schema). 7) Security aspects (auth, headers). 8) Boundary conditions. 9) Data consistency with DB.

content.title: Q12: How do you test authentication/authorization APIs?
content.explanation: Test scenarios: 1) Valid credentials -> success. 2) Invalid credentials -> 401. 3) Missing token -> 401. 4) Expired token -> 401. 5) Insufficient permissions -> 403. 6) Token refresh flow. 7) Multiple auth methods (Basic, OAuth2, JWT). 8) Rate limiting. Tools: Postman environment variables, automation with token management.

content.title: Q13: How would you automate an e-commerce checkout flow?
content.explanation: Approach: 1) Break into small testable units: login, product search, cart, address, payment, confirmation. 2) Use POM with pages for each step. 3) Implement test data management for products, users, payments. 4) Handle dynamic elements (product availability). 5) Mock payment gateway in test env. 6) Validate order confirmation, email, DB updates. 7) Cross-browser testing. 8) Performance checks.

content.title: Q14: Design testing strategy for a microservices architecture
content.explanation: Testing pyramid: 1) Unit tests for each service. 2) Contract tests (Pact) for API compatibility. 3) Integration tests for service interactions. 4) Component tests for individual services with dependencies mocked. 5) End-to-end tests for critical user journeys. 6) Performance tests for each service and overall. 7) Chaos engineering for resilience. Tools: Docker, Kubernetes, service mesh, API gateways.

content.title: Q15: How do you prioritize what to automate?
content.explanation: Consider: 1) Business criticality (revenue impact). 2) Frequency of use. 3) Risk assessment. 4) Stability of feature. 5) Manual effort required. 6) ROI calculation. 7) Test data availability. 8) Technical feasibility. Generally prioritize: smoke tests, critical path, high-risk features, frequently used functionality, regression suite.

content.title: Q16: Describe a time you improved test automation
content.explanation: Use STAR method: Situation (describe context), Task (what needed improvement), Action (specific steps taken - framework upgrade, parallel execution, better reporting, CI integration), Result (quantifiable outcomes - reduced execution time by X%, increased coverage by Y%, reduced flakiness). Highlight technical decisions and collaboration.

content.title: Q17: How do you handle disagreements with developers about test failures?
content.explanation: Professional approach: 1) Isolate and reproduce the issue. 2) Gather evidence (screenshots, logs, steps). 3) Approach collaboratively, not confrontationally. 4) Understand their perspective. 5) Discuss root cause, not blame. 6) Agree on definition of 'done'. 7) Use it as learning opportunity. 8) Document agreements for future reference.

content.title: Q18: How do you measure success of automation?
content.explanation: KPIs: 1) Test execution time reduction. 2) Test coverage (functional, code). 3) Defect escape rate. 4) Flakiness rate. 5) Maintenance effort. 6) ROI (time saved vs. development cost). 7) Early bug detection. 8) Release cycle time improvement. 9) Team productivity. 10) Confidence in releases.

content.explanation: Selenium WebDriver uses a client-server architecture: The client (your test code in Java/Python/etc.) sends HTTP requests via the JSON Wire Protocol (or W3C WebDriver Protocol) to a browser-specific driver (chromedriver, geckodriver). This driver communicates with the browser via vendor-specific automation APIs. Chromedriver uses Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), while Geckodriver uses Marionette for Firefox. Key components: 1) Language Bindings (Java, Python, C#) - provide API. 2) JSON Wire Protocol - RESTful web service using JSON over HTTP. 3) Browser Drivers - translate protocol commands to browser-specific actions. 4) Browsers - execute commands via native automation support. Important: WebDriver doesn't inject JavaScript but uses browser's built-in automation capabilities, making it more stable than Selenium RC.

content.title: Q2: Advanced Locator Strategies & Performance Optimization
content.explanation: Beyond basic locators: 1) CSS Selector Optimization: Use '>' for direct child (#parent > .child), '~' for general sibling, '+' for adjacent sibling. Performance: ID(1ms) < CSS(2ms) < XPath(3-5ms). 2) Dynamic Element Handling: Use relative XPath with axes: preceding-sibling::, following-sibling::, ancestor::, descendant::. Example: //button[text()='Submit']/following-sibling::input[@type='text']. 3) Custom Attributes: Work with devs to add data-testid attributes. 4) Shadow DOM: Use JavaScript execution: driver.executeScript('return document.querySelector("custom-element").shadowRoot.querySelector("button")'). 5) Iframes: Always switch context: driver.switchTo().frame(). 6) Performance: Cache elements, minimize DOM queries, use explicit waits with expected conditions like elementToBeClickable, visibilityOfElementLocated.

content.title: Q3: Comprehensive Wait Strategy Design Pattern
content.explanation: Robust wait implementation: 1) Explicit Wait Factory: Create custom ExpectedConditions for business logic. 2) Fluent Wait Configuration: Polling interval (500ms), timeout (30s), ignoring specific exceptions. 3) Page Load Strategy: Use driver.manage().timeouts().pageLoadTimeout(). 4) JavaScript Ready State: wait.until(d -> ((JavascriptExecutor)d).executeScript('return document.readyState').equals('complete')). 5) AJAX Completion: Wait for jQuery.active === 0. 6) Custom Conditions: Wait for element count, attribute value, CSS property. Implementation: public static WebElement waitForElementCustom(WebDriver driver, By locator, Function<WebDriver, Boolean> condition) { WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, Duration.ofSeconds(30)); wait.pollingEvery(Duration.ofMillis(500)); wait.ignoring(StaleElementReferenceException.class); return wait.until(d -> { if (condition.apply(d)) { return d.findElement(locator); } return null; }); }

import json
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import sqlite3
import numpy as np

class TestAnalyticsDashboard:
    def __init__(self, db_path="test_analytics.db"):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        self.create_tables()
    
    def create_tables(self):
        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
        
        # Test execution history
        cursor.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_executions (
            execution_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            timestamp DATETIME,
            test_suite TEXT,
            total_tests INTEGER,
            passed INTEGER,
            failed INTEGER,
            skipped INTEGER,
            execution_time REAL,
            environment TEXT,
            browser TEXT,
            success_rate REAL,
            flaky_tests INTEGER
        )''')
        
        # Test failure details
        cursor.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_failures (
            failure_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            execution_id TEXT,
            test_name TEXT,
            error_message TEXT,
            stack_trace TEXT,
            screenshot_path TEXT,
            failure_category TEXT,
            FOREIGN KEY (execution_id) REFERENCES test_executions (execution_id)
        )''')
        
        # Performance metrics
        cursor.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS performance_metrics (
            metric_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            timestamp DATETIME,
            endpoint TEXT,
            response_time REAL,
            throughput REAL,
            error_rate REAL,
            percentile_95 REAL,
            percentile_99 REAL
        )''')
        
        # Test coverage
        cursor.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_coverage (
            coverage_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            timestamp DATETIME,
            module_name TEXT,
            line_coverage REAL,
            branch_coverage REAL,
            code_complexity REAL
        )''')
        
        self.conn.commit()
    
    def add_test_execution(self, execution_data):
        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute('''INSERT INTO test_executions VALUES (
            :execution_id, :timestamp, :test_suite, :total_tests, :passed, 
            :failed, :skipped, :execution_time, :environment, :browser, 
            :success_rate, :flaky_tests
        )''', execution_data)
        self.conn.commit()
    
    def generate_execution_trends(self, days=30):
        query = f"""
        SELECT 
            DATE(timestamp) as date,
            test_suite,
            AVG(success_rate) as avg_success_rate,
            AVG(execution_time) as avg_execution_time,
            SUM(total_tests) as total_tests,
            SUM(failed) as total_failures
        FROM test_executions 
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-{days} days')
        GROUP BY DATE(timestamp), test_suite
        ORDER BY date
        """
        
        df = pd.read_sql_query(query, self.conn)
        return df
    
    def generate_comprehensive_dashboard(self):
        fig = make_subplots(
            rows=3, cols=3,
            subplot_titles=(
                'Test Success Rate Trend', 'Execution Time Trend',
                'Failure Distribution', 'Test Coverage',
                'Performance Metrics', 'Flaky Tests Trend',
                'Environment Comparison', 'Test Suite Health', 'ROI Analysis'
            ),
            specs=[
                [{'type': 'scatter'}, {'type': 'scatter'}, {'type': 'pie'}],
                [{'type': 'bar'}, {'type': 'indicator'}, {'type': 'scatter'}],
                [{'type': 'box'}, {'type': 'heatmap'}, {'type': 'bar'}]
            ],
            vertical_spacing=0.1,
            horizontal_spacing=0.1
        )
        
        # Get data for last 30 days
        trends_df = self.generate_execution_trends(30)
        
        # 1. Success Rate Trend
        for suite in trends_df['test_suite'].unique():
            suite_data = trends_df[trends_df['test_suite'] == suite]
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=suite_data['date'],
                    y=suite_data['avg_success_rate'],
                    name=suite,
                    mode='lines+markers',
                    line=dict(width=2)
                ),
                row=1, col=1
            )
        
        # 2. Execution Time Trend
        for suite in trends_df['test_suite'].unique():
            suite_data = trends_df[trends_df['test_suite'] == suite]
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=suite_data['date'],
                    y=suite_data['avg_execution_time'],
                    name=suite,
                    mode='lines+markers',
                    showlegend=False
                ),
                row=1, col=2
            )
        
        # 3. Failure Distribution
        failure_query = """
        SELECT failure_category, COUNT(*) as count
        FROM test_failures
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-30 days')
        GROUP BY failure_category
        """
        failure_df = pd.read_sql_query(failure_query, self.conn)
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Pie(
                labels=failure_df['failure_category'],
                values=failure_df['count'],
                hole=0.4,
                textinfo='label+percent'
            ),
            row=1, col=3
        )
        
        # 4. Test Coverage
        coverage_query = """
        SELECT module_name, AVG(line_coverage) as avg_coverage
        FROM test_coverage
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-7 days')
        GROUP BY module_name
        ORDER BY avg_coverage
        """
        coverage_df = pd.read_sql_query(coverage_query, self.conn)
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Bar(
                x=coverage_df['avg_coverage'],
                y=coverage_df['module_name'],
                orientation='h',
                marker_color='lightblue'
            ),
            row=2, col=1
        )
        
        # 5. Performance Metrics Indicator
        perf_query = """
        SELECT 
            AVG(response_time) as avg_response_time,
            AVG(percentile_95) as avg_p95,
            AVG(error_rate) as avg_error_rate
        FROM performance_metrics
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-1 day')
        """
        perf_df = pd.read_sql_query(perf_query, self.conn)
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Indicator(
                mode="gauge+number",
                value=perf_df['avg_response_time'].iloc[0],
                title={'text': "Avg Response Time (ms)"},
                domain={'x': [0, 1], 'y': [0, 1]},
                gauge={
                    'axis': {'range': [0, 2000]},
                    'bar': {'color': "darkblue"},
                    'steps': [
                        {'range': [0, 500], 'color': "green"},
                        {'range': [500, 1000], 'color': "yellow"},
                        {'range': [1000, 2000], 'color': "red"}
                    ],
                    'threshold': {
                        'line': {'color': "red", 'width': 4},
                        'thickness': 0.75,
                        'value': 1000
                    }
                }
            ),
            row=2, col=2
        )
        
        # 6. Flaky Tests Trend
        flaky_query = """
        SELECT 
            DATE(timestamp) as date,
            SUM(flaky_tests) as total_flaky
        FROM test_executions
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-30 days')
        GROUP BY DATE(timestamp)
        ORDER BY date
        """
        flaky_df = pd.read_sql_query(flaky_query, self.conn)
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=flaky_df['date'],
                y=flaky_df['total_flaky'],
                mode='lines+markers',
                name='Flaky Tests',
                line=dict(color='red', width=2),
                fill='tozeroy'
            ),
            row=2, col=3
        )
        
        # 7. Environment Comparison
        env_query = """
        SELECT 
            environment,
            AVG(success_rate) as success_rate,
            AVG(execution_time) as exec_time
        FROM test_executions
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-7 days')
        GROUP BY environment
        """
        env_df = pd.read_sql_query(env_query, self.conn)
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Box(
                y=env_df['success_rate'],
                x=env_df['environment'],
                name='Success Rate by Environment',
                boxpoints='all'
            ),
            row=3, col=1
        )
        
        # 8. Test Suite Health Heatmap
        heatmap_query = """
        SELECT 
            test_suite,
            DATE(timestamp) as date,
            success_rate
        FROM test_executions
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-14 days')
        """
        heatmap_df = pd.read_sql_query(heatmap_query, self.conn)
        
        # Pivot for heatmap
        pivot_df = heatmap_df.pivot(index='date', columns='test_suite', values='success_rate')
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Heatmap(
                z=pivot_df.values,
                x=pivot_df.columns,
                y=pivot_df.index,
                colorscale='RdYlGn',
                zmin=0,
                zmax=100
            ),
            row=3, col=2
        )
        
        # 9. ROI Analysis
        roi_query = """
        SELECT 
            DATE(timestamp) as date,
            SUM(total_tests) as automated_tests,
            SUM(execution_time) / 3600 as hours_saved
        FROM test_executions
        WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-30 days')
        GROUP BY DATE(timestamp)
        ORDER BY date
        """
        roi_df = pd.read_sql_query(roi_query, self.conn)
        
        # Calculate cumulative savings
        roi_df['cumulative_hours'] = roi_df['hours_saved'].cumsum()
        
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Bar(
                x=roi_df['date'],
                y=roi_df['cumulative_hours'],
                name='Cumulative Hours Saved',
                marker_color='green'
            ),
            row=3, col=3
        )
        
        # Update layout
        fig.update_layout(
            height=1200,
            title_text="Comprehensive Test Automation Dashboard",
            showlegend=True,
            template="plotly_white"
        )
        
        # Update axes
        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Date", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Success Rate (%)", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Date", row=1, col=2)
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Execution Time (s)", row=1, col=2)
        
        # Save dashboard
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        dashboard_file = f"reports/dashboard_{timestamp}.html"
        fig.write_html(dashboard_file)
        
        return dashboard_file
    
    def generate_executive_summary(self):
        """Generate executive summary report"""
        summary = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "metrics": {},
            "trends": {},
            "recommendations": []
        }
        
        # Calculate key metrics
        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
        
        # Overall success rate
        cursor.execute('''
            SELECT 
                AVG(success_rate) as overall_success_rate,
                COUNT(DISTINCT execution_id) as total_executions,
                SUM(total_tests) as total_tests_run,
                SUM(failed) as total_failures,
                SUM(execution_time) / 3600 as total_execution_hours
            FROM test_executions
            WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-30 days')
        ''')
        
        row = cursor.fetchone()
        summary["metrics"] = {
            "overall_success_rate": round(row[0], 2) if row[0] else 0,
            "total_executions": row[1] or 0,
            "total_tests_run": row[2] or 0,
            "total_failures": row[3] or 0,
            "total_execution_hours": round(row[4], 2) if row[4] else 0
        }
        
        # Success rate trend
        cursor.execute('''
            SELECT 
                AVG(CASE WHEN timestamp >= DATE('now', '-7 days') THEN success_rate END) as last_7_days,
                AVG(CASE WHEN timestamp >= DATE('now', '-14 days') AND timestamp < DATE('now', '-7 days') 
                    THEN success_rate END) as previous_7_days
            FROM test_executions
        ''')
        
        trend_row = cursor.fetchone()
        if trend_row[0] and trend_row[1]:
            trend = ((trend_row[0] - trend_row[1]) / trend_row[1]) * 100
            summary["trends"]["success_rate_trend"] = round(trend, 2)
        
        # Flaky tests analysis
        cursor.execute('''
            SELECT 
                AVG(flaky_tests) as avg_flaky_tests,
                MAX(flaky_tests) as max_flaky_tests
            FROM test_executions
            WHERE timestamp >= DATE('now', '-30 days')
        ''')
        
        flaky_row = cursor.fetchone()
        summary["metrics"]["avg_flaky_tests"] = round(flaky_row[0], 2) if flaky_row[0] else 0
        summary["metrics"]["max_flaky_tests"] = flaky_row[1] or 0
        
        # Generate recommendations
        if summary["metrics"]["overall_success_rate"] < 95:
            summary["recommendations"].append(
                f"Improve test success rate from {summary['metrics']['overall_success_rate']}% to 95%"
            )
        
        if summary["metrics"]["avg_flaky_tests"] > 5:
            summary["recommendations"].append(
                f"Investigate and fix {summary['metrics']['avg_flaky_tests']} flaky tests on average"
            )
        
        # Calculate ROI
        # Assuming manual testing would take 10 minutes per test case
        manual_testing_hours = (summary["metrics"]["total_tests_run"] * 10) / 60
        automation_hours = summary["metrics"]["total_execution_hours"]
        
        if automation_hours > 0:
            time_savings = manual_testing_hours - automation_hours
            summary["metrics"]["time_savings_hours"] = round(time_savings, 2)
            summary["metrics"]["roi_percentage"] = round((time_savings / automation_hours) * 100, 2)
        
        return summary

class IntelligentMobileAutomationFramework:

    def __init__(self, config_path: str = 'mobile_config.json'):
        self.config = self._load_config(config_path)
        self.drivers: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.device_manager = DeviceManager()
        self.ai_element_finder = AIElementFinder()
        self.visual_validator = MobileVisualValidator()
        self.performance_monitor = MobilePerformanceMonitor()
        
        # Session management
        self.active_sessions = {}

    async def initialize_driver(self, platform: str, device_config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """
        Initialize mobile driver with intelligent configuration
        based on platform and device characteristics.
        """
        
        # Generate capabilities using AI-powered optimization
        capabilities = self._generate_optimal_capabilities(platform, device_config)
        
        # Determine endpoint (local or cloud)
        endpoint = self._get_endpoint(device_config)
        
        try:
            if platform.lower() == 'android':
                driver = webdriver.Remote(
                    command_executor=endpoint,
                    options=AppiumOptions().load_capabilities(capabilities)
                )
            elif platform.lower() == 'ios':
                driver = webdriver.Remote(
                    command_executor=endpoint,
                    options=AppiumOptions().load_capabilities(capabilities)
                )
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported platform: {platform}")
            
            # Store driver reference
            driver_id = f"{platform}_{device_config['deviceName']}_{datetime.now().timestamp()}"
            self.drivers[driver_id] = {
                'driver': driver,
                'platform': platform,
                'capabilities': capabilities,
                'start_time': datetime.now(),
                'session_id': driver.session_id
            }
            
            # Initialize AI services for this session
            await self._initialize_ai_services(driver_id, driver)
            
            return driver
            
        except Exception as e:

            raise
    
    async def find_element_intelligently(self, driver_id: str, 
                                       locator_strategy: str, 
                                       locator_value: str,

        """
        Find mobile element using AI-enhanced strategies with
        self-healing capabilities.

        driver_info = self.drivers.get(driver_id)

            raise ValueError(f"Driver not found: {driver_id}")
        
        driver = driver_info['driver']

        # Primary attempt with standard locator

            self._record_locator_success(locator_strategy, locator_value, 'primary')
            return element
        except Exception as e:

        # AI-powered fallback strategies

            self._find_by_accessibility_hierarchy,
            self._find_by_relative_position,
            self._find_by_ocr_text_recognition

                    # Learn from successful recovery

                        driver_id, locator_strategy, locator_value, strategy.__name__
                    )
                    
                    # Suggest updated locator
                    new_locator = await self._suggest_better_locator(
                        element, driver, platform
                    )
                    
                    self.logger.info(f"Recovered element using {strategy.__name__}")
                    return element
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.debug(f"Strategy {strategy.__name__} failed: {str(e)}")
                continue
        
        # Last resort: visual search with template matching
        return await self._find_by_template_matching(driver, platform, locator_value, context)
    
    async def _find_by_visual_similarity(self, driver, platform: str, 
                                       target_description: str, 
                                       context: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Any]:
        """
        Find element using visual similarity matching with AI.
        """
        
        # Capture current screen
        screenshot = driver.get_screenshot_as_png()
        
        # Convert to OpenCV format
        nparr = np.frombuffer(screenshot, np.uint8)
        screen_image = cv2.imdecode(nparr, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        
        # Get target element signature from AI model
        target_signature = await self.ai_element_finder.get_element_signature(
            target_description, platform, context
        )
        
        # Use template matching with multiple methods
        methods = [cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, cv2.TM_CCORR_NORMED, cv2.TM_SQDIFF_NORMED]
        best_match = None
        best_confidence = 0
        
        for method in methods:
            result = cv2.matchTemplate(screen_image, target_signature, method)
            min_val, max_val, min_loc, max_loc = cv2.minMaxLoc(result)
            
            confidence = max_val if method in [cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, cv2.TM_CCORR_NORMED] else 1 - min_val
            
            if confidence > best_confidence and confidence > 0.7:
                best_confidence = confidence
                best_match = max_loc if method in [cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, cv2.TM_CCORR_NORMED] else min_loc
        
        if best_match and best_confidence > 0.8:
            # Convert screen coordinates to element
            x, y = best_match
            element = driver.execute_script("""
                return document.elementFromPoint(arguments[0], arguments[1]);
            """, x, y)
            
            return element
        
        return None

    async def _execute_testing_stage(self, trigger_event: Dict[str, Any],

        """
        
        test_stage_result = {

            # Calculate overall metrics

    async def _execute_tests_in_parallel(self, selected_tests: Dict[str, Any], 
                                       build_result: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Execute tests in parallel across multiple devices/platforms.
        """
        
        execution_result = {
            'overall_success': True,
            'tests_executed': 0,
            'tests_passed': 0,
            'tests_failed': 0,
            'tests_skipped': 0,
            'devices_used': [],
            'device_results': {},
            'parallel_efficiency': 0
        }
        
        # Get available devices from device farm
        available_devices = await self._get_available_devices(selected_tests)
        
        # Distribute tests across devices
        test_distribution = await self._distribute_tests_across_devices(
            selected_tests['selected_tests'], 
            available_devices
        )
        
        # Execute tests in parallel
        tasks = []
        for device_id, device_tests in test_distribution.items():
            task = self._execute_tests_on_device(device_id, device_tests, build_result)
            tasks.append(task)
        
        # Wait for all device executions to complete
        device_results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        
        # Aggregate results
        for i, (device_id, device_tests) in enumerate(test_distribution.items()):
            device_result = device_results[i]
            
            if isinstance(device_result, Exception):
                execution_result['device_results'][device_id] = {
                    'success': False,
                    'error': str(device_result)
                }
                execution_result['overall_success'] = False
            else:
                execution_result['device_results'][device_id] = device_result
                execution_result['tests_executed'] += device_result['tests_executed']
                execution_result['tests_passed'] += device_result['tests_passed']
                execution_result['tests_failed'] += device_result['tests_failed']
                execution_result['tests_skipped'] += device_result['tests_skipped']
                execution_result['devices_used'].append(device_id)
                
                if not device_result['success']:
                    execution_result['overall_success'] = False
        
        # Calculate parallel efficiency
        total_execution_time = max(
            result.get('execution_time', 0) 
            for result in execution_result['device_results'].values() 
            if not isinstance(result, Exception)
        )
        
        if total_execution_time > 0:
            total_test_time = sum(
                result.get('total_test_time', 0)
                for result in execution_result['device_results'].values()
                if not isinstance(result, Exception)
            )
            execution_result['parallel_efficiency'] = total_test_time / (
                total_execution_time * len(execution_result['devices_used'])
            )
        
        execution_result['pass_rate'] = (
            execution_result['tests_passed'] / execution_result['tests_executed'] 
            if execution_result['tests_executed'] > 0 else 0
        )
        
        return execution_result

        """

        """
        
        generated_tests = {
            'app_package': app_package,
            'platform': platform,
            'generation_time': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'test_categories': {},
            'coverage_metrics': {},
            'recommendations': []

        try:
            # Phase 1: App Exploration and Screen Analysis
            exploration_result = await self._explore_app(
                app_package, platform, exploration_time
            )
            
            generated_tests['exploration_data'] = exploration_result
            
            # Phase 2: Screen Understanding and Component Identification
            screen_analysis = await self.screen_analyzer.analyze_screens(
                exploration_result['screens'], platform
            )
            
            generated_tests['screen_analysis'] = screen_analysis
            
            # Phase 3: User Flow Learning
            user_flows = await self.flow_learner.learn_user_flows(
                exploration_result['interaction_logs'],

            )
            
            generated_tests['learned_user_flows'] = user_flows
            
            # Phase 4: Test Scenario Generation
            test_scenarios = await self.test_scenario_generator.generate_scenarios(
                screen_analysis,

            )
            
            generated_tests['generated_scenarios'] = test_scenarios
            
            # Phase 5: Test Code Generation
            test_code = await self.test_code_generator.generate_test_code(

            )
            
            generated_tests['executable_tests'] = test_code
            
            # Calculate coverage metrics

                screen_analysis,

            )

            # Generate recommendations
            recommendations = self._generate_test_recommendations(
                screen_analysis,

            generated_tests['recommendations'] = recommendations
            
            # Categorize tests

            generated_tests['test_categories'] = categorized_tests
            
        except Exception as e:

    async def _explore_app(self, app_package: str, platform: str, 
                         exploration_time: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Explore the mobile app to understand its structure and flows.
        """
        
        exploration_data = {
            'screens': [],
            'interaction_logs': [],
            'navigation_graph': {},
            'discovered_features': [],
            'exploration_coverage': 0
        }
        
        # Initialize exploration
        exploration_session = await self._start_exploration_session(app_package, platform)
        
        start_time = time.time()
        visited_screens = set()
        
        while time.time() - start_time < exploration_time:
            # Capture current screen
            current_screen = await self._capture_screen(exploration_session)
            screen_hash = self._calculate_screen_hash(current_screen)
            
            if screen_hash not in visited_screens:
                # Analyze new screen
                screen_analysis = await self._analyze_screen(current_screen, platform)
                exploration_data['screens'].append(screen_analysis)
                visited_screens.add(screen_hash)
                
                # Discover interactive elements
                interactive_elements = await self._discover_interactive_elements(
                    current_screen, platform
                )
                
                # Explore interactions
                for element in interactive_elements:
                    interaction_result = await self._explore_interaction(
                        exploration_session, element
                    )
                    
                    exploration_data['interaction_logs'].append({
                        'from_screen': screen_hash,
                        'element': element,
                        'result': interaction_result,
                        'timestamp': time.time()
                    })
                    
                    # Update navigation graph
                    self._update_navigation_graph(
                        exploration_data['navigation_graph'],
                        screen_hash,
                        interaction_result
                    )
            
            # Explore random navigation to increase coverage
            await self._explore_random_navigation(exploration_session)
            
            # Check for new features
            new_features = await self._discover_new_features(current_screen)
            exploration_data['discovered_features'].extend(new_features)
            
        # Calculate exploration coverage
        exploration_data['exploration_coverage'] = len(visited_screens) / self._estimate_total_screens(app_package)
        
        await self._end_exploration_session(exploration_session)
        
        return exploration_data

        elif execution_strategy['type'] == 'circuit_breaker':

        elif execution_strategy['type'] == 'load_balanced':

        if auth_type == 'none':

        # Check cache for valid tokens
        cached_auth = await self.token_cache.get(auth_config, context)
        if cached_auth and self._is_token_valid(cached_auth):
            return cached_auth
        
        # Get appropriate auth provider
        provider = self.auth_providers.get(auth_type)
        if not provider:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported auth type: {auth_type}")
        
        # Perform authentication
        auth_result = await provider.authenticate(auth_config, context)
        
        # Analyze security aspects
        security_analysis = await self.security_analyzer.analyze(auth_result, auth_config)
        auth_result['security_analysis'] = security_analysis
        
        # Cache the result

        # Generate authentication insights
        insights = await self._generate_auth_insights(auth_result, auth_config)
        auth_result['insights'] = insights
        
        return auth_result
    
    async def refresh_token(self, auth_config: Dict[str, Any], 
                          context: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Refresh authentication token intelligently.
        """
        
        auth_type = auth_config.get('type')
        provider = self.auth_providers.get(auth_type)
        
        if not provider or not hasattr(provider, 'refresh_token'):
            # Fall back to re-authentication
            await self.token_cache.invalidate(auth_config, context)
            return await self.authenticate(auth_config, context)
        
        # Attempt token refresh
        try:
            refreshed = await provider.refresh_token(auth_config, context)
            
            # Update cache
            await self.token_cache.set(auth_config, refreshed, context)
            
            return refreshed
            
        except Exception as e:
            # If refresh fails, re-authenticate
            await self.token_cache.invalidate(auth_config, context)
            return await self.authenticate(auth_config, context)

    name: Static Performance Analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Run static performance analysis
      uses: performance-ai/static-analyzer@v1
      with:
        language: 'javascript'
        ruleset: 'performance-best-practices'
    
    - name: Upload analysis results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: static-performance-analysis
        path: performance-analysis-report.json
  
  quick-smoke-tests:
    name: Quick Smoke Performance Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: performance-analysis
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: '18'
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci
    
    - name: Run quick smoke tests
      uses: k6io/action@v0.2
      with:
        filename: tests/performance/smoke-test.js
        flags: --out cloud
        cloud: true
        cloud-project-id: ${{ secrets.K6_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID }}
    
    - name: Analyze smoke test results
      uses: performance-ai/test-analyzer@v1
      with:
        test-type: 'smoke'
        threshold-file: 'performance-thresholds.json'
    
    - name: Notify on failure
      if: failure()
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: failure
        text: 'Performance smoke test failed for PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}'
  
  api-load-tests:
    name: API Load Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quick-smoke-tests
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup load test environment
      run: |
        docker-compose -f docker-compose.performance.yml up -d
        sleep 30  # Wait for services to start
    
    - name: Run comprehensive load tests
      uses: k6io/action@v0.2
      with:
        filename: tests/performance/load-test.js
        flags: |
          --out influxdb=http://localhost:8086/k6
          --out cloud
          --tag environment=${{ env.PERFORMANCE_ENVIRONMENT }}
          --tag commit=${{ github.sha }}
        cloud: true
        cloud-project-id: ${{ secrets.K6_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID }}
    
    - name: Collect and analyze metrics
      uses: performance-ai/metrics-collector@v1
      with:
        apm-provider: 'newrelic'
        metrics: 'response_time,throughput,error_rate'
    
    - name: Run AI-powered analysis
      uses: performance-ai/insights-engine@v1
      with:
        historical-data: 'performance-history.json'
        generate-recommendations: true
    
    - name: Upload performance report
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: load-test-report
        path: performance-report.html
  
  performance-gates:
    name: Performance Quality Gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: api-load-tests
    if: always()
    
    steps:
    - name: Download test results
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: load-test-report
    
    - name: Evaluate performance gates

      with:
        baseline-file: 'performance-baseline.json'
        current-results: 'performance-report.html'
        gates:
          - metric: 'p95_response_time'
            threshold: 500
            operator: '<'
          - metric: 'error_rate'
            threshold: 1
            operator: '<'
          - metric: 'throughput'
            threshold: 1000
            operator: '>'
        ai-adjustment: true
    
    - name: Generate performance insights
      uses: performance-ai/insights-generator@v1
      with:
        format: 'slack'
        channel: '#performance-alerts'
    
    - name: Update performance baseline
      if: success()
      uses: performance-ai/baseline-updater@v1
      with:
        current-results: 'performance-report.html'
        baseline-file: 'performance-baseline.json'
        learning-rate: 0.1
  
  endurance-tests:
    name: Endurance Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: performance-gates
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    
    steps:
    - name: Run 2-hour endurance test
      uses: k6io/action@v0.2
      with:
        filename: tests/performance/endurance-test.js
        flags: |
          --duration 2h
          --vus 100
          --out cloud
          --tag test-type=endurance
        cloud: true
    
    - name: Analyze memory leak patterns
      uses: performance-ai/memory-analyzer@v1
      with:
        duration: '2h'
        metrics: 'heap_usage,gc_pause'
    
    - name: Generate endurance report
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: endurance-test-report
        path: endurance-report.json
  
  performance-dashboard:
    name: Update Performance Dashboard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [performance-gates, endurance-tests]
    if: always()
    
    steps:
    - name: Update performance dashboard
      uses: performance-ai/dashboard-updater@v1
      with:
        dashboard-id: 'performance-metrics'
        data-source: 'influxdb'
        metrics:
          - response_time
          - throughput
          - error_rate
          - resource_utilization
    
    - name: Send summary to Slack
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: ${{ job.status }}
        text: |
          Performance pipeline completed for commit ${{ github.sha }}
          
          Results:
          - Smoke Tests: ${{ needs.quick-smoke-tests.result }}
          - Load Tests: ${{ needs.api-load-tests.result }}

    and intelligent analysis.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
        self.config = config
        self.history_manager = PerformanceHistoryManager()
        self.anomaly_detector = AnomalyDetector()
        self.trend_analyzer = TrendAnalyzer()
        self.risk_assessor = RiskAssessor()
        
        # ML models
        self.threshold_model = self._train_threshold_model()
        self.prediction_model = self._train_prediction_model()
        
    async def evaluate_gates(self, 
                           current_metrics: List[PerformanceMetric], 
                           context: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Evaluate all performance quality gates intelligently.
        """
        
        gate_results = {
            'evaluation_time': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'context': context,
            'gates': [],
            'overall_result': 'PASS',
            'confidence_score': 0.0,
            'insights': [],
            'recommendations': []
        }
        
        # Get historical data for context
        historical_data = await self.history_manager.get_relevant_history(
            current_metrics, 
            context
        )
        
        # Evaluate each metric gate
        for metric in current_metrics:
            gate_result = await self._evaluate_single_gate(
                metric, 
                historical_data, 
                context
            )
            gate_results['gates'].append(gate_result)
            
            if not gate_result.passed:
                if gate_result.severity == 'critical':
                    gate_results['overall_result'] = 'FAIL'
                elif gate_results['overall_result'] == 'PASS':
                    gate_results['overall_result'] = 'WARNING'
        
        # Perform multi-metric correlation analysis
        correlation_analysis = await self._analyze_metric_correlations(
            current_metrics, 
            historical_data
        )
        gate_results['correlation_analysis'] = correlation_analysis
        
        # Generate overall insights
        insights = await self._generate_overall_insights(
            gate_results['gates'], 
            correlation_analysis, 
            context
        )
        gate_results['insights'] = insights
        
        # Calculate overall confidence
        confidence = self._calculate_overall_confidence(gate_results)
        gate_results['confidence_score'] = confidence
        
        # Generate recommendations
        recommendations = await self._generate_recommendations(gate_results, context)
        gate_results['recommendations'] = recommendations
        
        # Learn from this evaluation
        await self._learn_from_evaluation(gate_results, context)
        
        return gate_results
    
    async def _evaluate_single_gate(self, 
                                  metric: PerformanceMetric,
                                  historical_data: Dict[str, Any],
                                  context: Dict[str, Any]) -> QualityGateResult:
        """
        Evaluate a single performance metric gate.
        """
        
        # Get adaptive threshold
        threshold = await self._get_adaptive_threshold(metric, historical_data, context)
        
        # Check against threshold
        if metric.unit == 'ms' and metric.name.endswith('_response_time'):
            # Lower is better for response time
            passed = metric.value <= threshold['value']
            deviation = (metric.value - threshold['value']) / threshold['value'] * 100
        elif metric.name.endswith('_rate') or metric.name.endswith('_percentage'):
            # Check based on threshold direction
            if threshold.get('direction') == 'lower':
                passed = metric.value <= threshold['value']
            else:
                passed = metric.value >= threshold['value']
            deviation = abs(metric.value - threshold['value']) / threshold['value'] * 100
        else:
            # Default comparison
            passed = metric.value <= threshold['value']
            deviation = (metric.value - threshold['value']) / threshold['value'] * 100
        
        # Detect anomalies
        is_anomaly = await self.anomaly_detector.detect(
            metric.value,
            historical_data.get(metric.name, []),
            context
        )
        
        # Analyze trend
        trend = await self.trend_analyzer.analyze(
            metric.value,
            historical_data.get(metric.name, []),
            context
        )
        
        # Assess risk
        risk_assessment = await self.risk_assessor.assess(
            metric,
            passed,
            deviation,
            is_anomaly,
            trend,
            context
        )
        
        # Calculate confidence
        confidence = self._calculate_gate_confidence(
            passed, deviation, is_anomaly, trend, risk_assessment
        )
        
        # Generate recommendation
        recommendation = await self._generate_gate_recommendation(
            metric,
            passed,
            deviation,
            is_anomaly,
            trend,
            risk_assessment
        )
        
        # Determine severity
        severity = self._determine_severity(
            passed, deviation, is_anomaly, risk_assessment
        )
        
        return QualityGateResult(
            gate_name=metric.name,
            passed=passed,
            confidence=confidence,
            actual_value=metric.value,
            expected_value=threshold['value'],
            deviation=deviation,
            recommendation=recommendation,
            severity=severity
        )
    
    async def _get_adaptive_threshold(self, 
                                    metric: PerformanceMetric,
                                    historical_data: Dict[str, Any],
                                    context: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Get adaptive threshold for a performance metric.
        """
        
        # Get baseline from configuration
        baseline_threshold = self.config.get('thresholds', {}).get(metric.name, {})
        
        if not baseline_threshold:
            # Infer threshold from historical data
            historical_values = historical_data.get(metric.name, [])
            if historical_values:
                values = [h['value'] for h in historical_values]
                
                # Use percentiles for dynamic threshold
                if metric.unit == 'ms' and metric.name.endswith('_response_time'):
                    # For response time, use p95 + 20% buffer
                    threshold_value = np.percentile(values, 95) * 1.2
                    direction = 'lower'
                else:
                    # For rates, use historical average
                    threshold_value = np.mean(values)
                    direction = baseline_threshold.get('direction', 'lower')
            else:
                # No historical data, use default
                threshold_value = baseline_threshold.get('value', 1000)
                direction = baseline_threshold.get('direction', 'lower')
        else:
            threshold_value = baseline_threshold['value']
            direction = baseline_threshold.get('direction', 'lower')
        
        # Adjust based on context
        context_adjustment = await self._adjust_for_context(
            threshold_value, 
            metric, 
            context
        )
        
        # Apply ML-based prediction
        predicted_threshold = await self._predict_optimal_threshold(
            metric, 
            historical_data, 
            context
        )
        
        # Combine adjustments
        final_threshold = {
            'value': predicted_threshold or context_adjustment or threshold_value,
            'direction': direction,
            'confidence': self._calculate_threshold_confidence(
                threshold_value, 
                historical_data, 
                context
            ),
            'adjustment_factors': {
                'baseline': baseline_threshold,
                'context_adjustment': context_adjustment,
                'ml_prediction': predicted_threshold
            }
        }
        
        return final_threshold
    
    async def _predict_optimal_threshold(self, 
                                       metric: PerformanceMetric,
                                       historical_data: Dict[str, Any],
                                       context: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[float]:
        """
        Use ML to predict optimal threshold for current context.
        """
        
        # Prepare features for prediction
        features = self._extract_prediction_features(metric, historical_data, context)
        
        if len(features) < 10:
            # Not enough data for reliable prediction
            return None
        
        # Use trained model to predict threshold
        predicted_value = self.threshold_model.predict([features])[0]
        
        # Apply confidence bounds
        confidence_interval = self._calculate_confidence_interval(features)
        
        return predicted_value * confidence_interval
    
    async def _analyze_metric_correlations(self, 
                                         current_metrics: List[PerformanceMetric],
                                         historical_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Analyze correlations between different performance metrics.
        """
        
        correlation_analysis = {
            'strong_correlations': [],
            'unexpected_patterns': [],
            'causality_hints': [],
            'insights': []
        }
        
        # Create metric matrix
        metric_matrix = {}
        for metric in current_metrics:
            metric_matrix[metric.name] = metric.value
        
        # Get historical correlations
        historical_correlations = self.history_manager.get_correlations()
        
        # Check for expected correlations
        for metric1, metric2, expected_correlation in historical_correlations:
            if metric1 in metric_matrix and metric2 in metric_matrix:
                actual_correlation = self._calculate_correlation(
                    metric_matrix[metric1], 
                    metric_matrix[metric2]
                )
                
                if abs(actual_correlation - expected_correlation) > 0.3:
                    correlation_analysis['unexpected_patterns'].append({
                        'metrics': [metric1, metric2],
                        'expected_correlation': expected_correlation,
                        'actual_correlation': actual_correlation,
                        'deviation': abs(actual_correlation - expected_correlation)
                    })
                
                if abs(actual_correlation) > 0.7:
                    correlation_analysis['strong_correlations'].append({
                        'metrics': [metric1, metric2],
                        'correlation': actual_correlation
                    })
        
        # Look for causality hints
        for pattern in correlation_analysis['strong_correlations']:
            if pattern['correlation'] > 0.8:
                # Strong positive correlation - might indicate causality
                causality_hint = await self._investigate_causality(
                    pattern['metrics'], 
                    metric_matrix, 
                    historical_data
                )
                if causality_hint:
                    correlation_analysis['causality_hints'].append(causality_hint)
        
        return correlation_analysis
